questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Firstly, that the university had a lot of intersting courses to choose from and it was a big plus if the country was well english-speaking. Moreover, that the academic level known to be good. Additionally, I wanted to experience new cultures and I had never been to Ireland before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The UCC website provides a lot of valuable information. Also, they were quick to answer any questions by e-mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received information about the orientation days which was enough for me, as we had the chance to ask questions and learn practical information on the orientation days. The student administration office was also very helpful with any inquiries you had.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation days were quite short. However, the UCC Societies did a lot of orientation and social events which was nice.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: On the UCC website, they list a number of on-campus and off-campus student accomodations and key information such as price, availability and contact information. This was very helpful, as accomodation generally in Cork is super difficult to get your hands on.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared a kitchen with other students at a student accomodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is quite expensive but a great way to get to know other students and be social.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of great student accomodations were available. However, it is important to be proactive well in advance of your exchange.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I received information on e-mail on all the steps and dates to register etc. and it was not a difficult process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UCC sends you an e-mail with a link to UCC and the steps provided in the e-mail are easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Before arriving, all communication was with a UCC coordinator and he was prompt in replying to your questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted, except for one "placement" class which was not available for visiting students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have two lists of courses; "Book of Modules" and "Book of Modules for visiting students". There are no law courses to choose from on the visiting students list due to a technical error. Instead, you have to choose from the law courses on "Book of Modules".

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good lectures and a big plus that they were all recorded and available to go through later on.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Since Ireland is a common law country there is a lot more focus on case law, and the doctrines and principles are different in contract law. However, there are many similarities and it is helpful to try to compare them to the danish equivalents.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some courses were in a classroom with discussion while others were in big lecture halls with hundreds of people. This varies from course to course so I advice that you research about such information on the courses if you prefer either or.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Law of Contract 2) Introduction to Business Law 3) Sale, Insurance and Carriage of Goods at Sea 4) Negotiation and Mediation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Negotiation and Mediation was very interesting, as I had not yet had any courses on means of alternative dispute resolution before. We were not many students and the lectures were in a classroom. I expecially liked that we did in-class simulation exercises which helped with the learning and getting to know the other students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was generally a bit more affordable while housing was more expensive than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UCC has a lot of societies, clubs and events that are active. This was a very nice addition to the exchange.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a bunch of different social clubs (Societies) and sport/athletic clubs (Clubs), for example football, handball, boxing, kickboxing, athletics, swimming, mountaineering, dancing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be active in one or two student clubs or societies. Moreover, go to Mardyke Arena which has swimming, climbing and three gyms available for students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on one or two day trips around Ireland. There are a bunch of different small and a nice atmosphere. Also, the nature is beatiful and I recommend that you go hike.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People are very nice and they all want to make friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Definitely to go to events of societies or clubs, including the organized trips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are very friendly and open.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look for accommodation as soon as you can. The rest is less of a hurdle.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open and outgoing, talk to people. Also, make an overview of lectures, deadlines and exam periods to better organize your social calendar around it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to know so many different people from different cultures, including law students. The lectures were also very interesting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
